concepts.label: Client-Side Retry Orchestration (RetryStrategy, RetryReason, idempotency-gated retries, pre-exception decision layer)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - this is a structurally distinct primitive from sdk:error-handling. sdk:error-handling is about which typed exception a request terminates with (a many-server-error-codes-to-one-exception-type mapping); RetryStrategy/RetryReason/idempotency operate BEFORE that point, deciding whether a request is retried transparently at all and never becomes a visible exception. The page states this ordering explicitly: 'With the SDK retrying all transparently retryable exceptions already ... you are only left with terminal exceptions.' Retryability is also gated by a request-shape property (idempotent vs non-idempotent) that has no counterpart in the exception-taxonomy concept.

notable_absence.finding: This page never links to kv-operations.md, even though its own worked examples are entirely KV-based (collection.get(), collection.upsert(), DocumentNotFoundException) and it explicitly says 'Please refer to each individual method (javadoc) for more information about which exceptions are thrown' rather than cross-referencing the howto page that documents those same methods. Also notable: this page contains zero mentions of transactions, TransactionFailedException, or TransactionCommitAmbiguousException - the transaction-specific exceptions covered later in this batch live entirely on a separate page (concept-docs/transactions-error-handling.md, linked from distributed-acid-transactions-from-the-sdk.md, not from here).

cross_component_finding: sdk:error-handling (the CouchbaseException hierarchy) and this page's RetryStrategy/RetryReason/idempotency machinery are related but genuinely separate SDK primitives operating at different points in the request lifecycle - one classifies terminal failures, the other decides whether a failure becomes terminal at all. I minted sdk:retry-strategy rather than folding it into sdk:error-handling, since the page itself frames retry decisions as happening strictly before exception classification, and idempotency (a property of the operation, not of an error code) is central to the retry decision in a way that has no analogue in the error-to-exception mapping.
